question: max number of paracetmol 500mg tabs an adult can take in 24 hrs according to the leaflet?
text:
According to the leaflet, an adult should not take more than 4000 mg (8 tablets of 500 mg) of paracetamol in any 24-hour period. [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Dosage-And-Administration]

This is equivalent to taking 1 to 2 tablets (500 mg to 1000 mg) every 4 to 6 hours when needed, with at least 4 hours between doses. [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Dosage-And-Administration]

It is also important to note that taking more than the stated dose will not give faster or better relief, and can be dangerous. [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Dosage-And-Administration]

Additionally, it is recommended to check the ingredients on the label of every cold or flu product before use, as taking more than one paracetamol-containing product can cause an accidental overdose and severe liver damage (hepatotoxicity). [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Warnings-And-Precautions]

question: does the paracetamol leaflet say anything about drinking alcohol or taking cold meds at the same time?
text:
Yes, the paracetamol leaflet warns that taking paracetamol together with any other medicine that contains paracetamol, including cold and flu remedies, can cause an accidental overdose and severe liver damage [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Warnings-And-Precautions]. It also advises checking the ingredients on the label of every cold or flu product before use.

Additionally, the leaflet notes that chronic heavy alcohol use increases the risk of liver toxicity and recommends consulting a doctor or pharmacist before taking paracetamol if you drink alcohol regularly and heavily [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Warnings-And-Precautions].

question: Wait which patients should NOT take ibuprofen according to our product leaflet?
text:

1. You have an active stomach or peptic ulcer, a history of recurrent peptic ulcers, or gastrointestinal bleeding. [ibuprofen_leaflet.md#Contraindications]
2. You have a known hypersensitivity to ibuprofen, or you have had asthma, wheezing or an allergic reaction triggered by aspirin or other NSAIDs. [ibuprofen_leaflet.md#Contraindications]
3. You are in the third trimester of pregnancy. [ibuprofen_leaflet.md#Contraindications]

These conditions make it unsafe for patients to take ibuprofen, and they should consult a pharmacist or doctor for a suitable alternative.
